items.title: 5.7 Area of a Triangular Region Whose Vertices are Given (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 157-158: 5.7 Area of a Triangular Region, trapezium derivation (Figure 5.10), Note box, determinant formula, Corollary, Examples 14-15

blocks.text: Ab tak hum ne triangle ka area hamesha 'half base into height' se nikala hai. Lekin agar sirf teen kone (vertices) ke coordinates diye hon, to base aur height naapna mushkil ho jata hai, kyunke height ke liye perpendicular ki lambai chahiye. Is sabaq mein hum ek aisa formula banayenge jo seedha coordinates se area de deta hai. Aur bonus: isi formula se pata chal jata hai ke teen points ek line par hain ya nahi.
Kitab ki shuruat: humein us triangular region ka area chahiye jis ke vertices \(P(x_1, y_1)\), \(Q(x_2, y_2)\) aur \(R(x_3, y_3)\) hain.
Teeno points se \(x\)-axis par perpendicular \(\overline{PL}\), \(\overline{QN}\) aur \(\overline{RM}\) giraiye. (Perpendicular yani seedhi khari line jo axis se \(90^\circ\) banaye.)

blocks.alt: Coordinate axes with origin O. A shaded triangle with vertices P(x1, y1) on the left, R(x3, y3) at the top and Q(x2, y2) on the right. Dashed perpendiculars PL, RM and QN drop to the x-axis, with heights y1, y3, y2. Below the axis, LM is marked x3 minus x1, MN is x2 minus x3, and LN is x2 minus x1.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.10: triangle PQR with perpendiculars PL, RM, QN to the x-axis (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Ab figure ko dekh kar kitab yeh relation likhti hai: triangle \(PQR\) ka area = trapezium \(PLMR\) ka area + trapezium \(RMNQ\) ka area \(-\) trapezium \(PLNQ\) ka area.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text:
Trapezium (trapezoid) aisi chaar sides wali shakal hai jis ki do sides parallel hon aur do parallel na hon.
Trapezium ka area \(= \frac{1}{2}\)(parallel sides ka jama)(parallel sides ke darmiyan faasla).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Trapezium hi kyun? \(PLMR\), \(RMNQ\), \(PLNQ\) teeno ki do sides khari (vertical) perpendiculars hain, aur khari lines aapas mein parallel hoti hain. In ki lambai seedhi \(y\)-coordinates hain, aur in ke darmiyan faasla \(x\)-axis par naapa jata hai, yani \(x\)-coordinates ka farq. Is tarah har cheez coordinates mein likhi ja sakti hai.
Figure 5.10 ko ghaur se dekhiye: upar wale do trapeziums mil kar triangle aur us ke neeche wala trapezium \(PLNQ\) dono ko dhak lete hain. \(PLNQ\) ko nikal dein to sirf triangle bachta hai. Bilkul aise jaise kisi zameen ke naqshe mein bara hissa naap kar faltu hissa minus kar dete hain.
Figure mein points \(x\)-axis ke upar hain aur \(x_1 < x_3 < x_2\); lekin aakhri formula har position ke liye sahi hai.
Ab har trapezium par Note wala formula lagate hain aur lambaiyan coordinates mein likhte hain:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Har line kahan se aayi: \(|\overline{PL}| = y_1\), \(|\overline{RM}| = y_3\), \(|\overline{QN}| = y_2\) (yeh points ki unchaiyan hain), aur \(|\overline{LM}| = x_3 - x_1\), \(|\overline{MN}| = x_2 - x_3\), \(|\overline{LN}| = x_2 - x_1\) (yeh axis par faasle hain).
Phir brackets khole. Ghaur karein: \(x_3y_3\), \(x_1y_1\) aur \(x_2y_2\) har ek ek dafa plus aur ek dafa minus aata hai, is liye cancel ho jate hain. Sirf chhe (6) terms bachte hain.
Is tarah required area yeh hai:

blocks.text_alt: Delta equals one half of: x1 times (y2 minus y3), plus x2 times (y3 minus y1), plus x3 times (y1 minus y2)

blocks.latex: \Delta = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}
blocks.text_alt: Delta equals one half of the determinant with rows x1 y1 1, x2 y2 1, x3 y3 1

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Determinant wahi cheez kyun deta hai? Isay teesre column (jis mein sab 1 hain) ke saath expand karein: \(1(x_2y_3 - x_3y_2) - 1(x_1y_3 - x_3y_1) + 1(x_1y_2 - x_2y_1)\). Yeh bilkul wahi chhe terms hain jo upar bache the. Determinant yaad rakhna aasaan hai: har row mein ek point aur aakhir mein 1.
Sign ka maamla: agar \(P \to Q \to R\) anticlockwise chalein (jaise Figure 5.10 mein) to jawab positive aata hai, clockwise chalein to negative. Area kabhi negative nahi hota, is liye negative jawab aaye to us ki absolute value le lein.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar aap \(P\) aur \(Q\) ki rows aapas mein badal dein to determinant ka kya hoga? (Jawab: sirf sign badlega, kyunke do rows badalne se determinant ka sign ulta ho jata hai. Area wahi rahega.)
Corollary
Agar points \(P\), \(Q\) aur \(R\) collinear (ek hi line par) hon, to \(\Delta = 0\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Ek hi line par pare teen points koi jagah gherte hi nahi, is liye area zero. Ulti baat bhi sahi hai: agar \(\Delta = 0\) aaye to points collinear hain. Is se collinearity check karne ka bohat tez tareeqa mil jata hai, jo Example 15 mein istemal hota hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Points \(A(0, 0)\), \(B(1, 1)\), \(C(5, 5)\) ka area kitna hoga, hisaab lagaye beghair? (Ishara: teeno points line \(y = x\) par hain. Is liye area zero hoga, aur formula se bhi \(\frac{1}{2}[0 + 1(5 - 0) + 5(0 - 1)] = 0\) aata hai.)

Ab kitab ki do misaalein. Pehli mein coordinates letters mein hain, doosri mein numbers hain aur jawab ek dilchasp natija deta hai. Dono mein ek hi tareeqa chalega: pehle determinant theek tarteeb se likhna, phir expand karna, aur aakhir mein jawab ko kisi doosre tareeqe se check karna.

blocks.title: Example 14
blocks.problem: Find the area of the region bounded by the triangle with vertices \(A(a, b)\), \(B(-a, b)\) and \(C(0, -b)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(a, b)\), \(B(-a, b)\), \(C(0, -b)\).
Maloom karna: triangle \(ABC\) ka area \(\Delta\).
Tareeqa: determinant wala formula \(\Delta = \frac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\). Har row mein ek vertex ke coordinates aur aakhir mein 1. Yahan coordinates letters mein hain, lekin tareeqa wohi hai jo numbers ke saath hota hai.

Qadam 1: determinant likhein
\[\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} a & b & 1 \\ -a & b & 1 \\ 0 & -b & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: rows mein \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) isi tarteeb se rakhe.

Qadam 2: pehli row ke saath expand karein
\[= \tfrac{1}{2}\big[a(b + b) - b(-a - 0)\]
\[+ 1(ab - 0)\big]\]
Kyun: row ke saath signs \(+, -, +\) chalte hain. \(a\) ka minor: \(b \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot (-b) = b + b\). \(b\) ka minor: \(-a \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 0 = -a\). 1 ka minor: \((-a)(-b) - b \cdot 0 = ab\).
Dhyan dein: beech wale term ke aage minus sign zaroor lagayein; isi jagah sab se zyada ghaltiyan hoti hain.

Qadam 3: simplify karein
\[= \tfrac{1}{2}\big[2ab + ab + ab\big]\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{2}(4ab) = 2ab\]
Kyun: \(-b \times (-a) = +ab\), minus aur minus mil kar plus.

Tasdeeq:
\(A\) aur \(B\) dono line \(y = b\) par hain, is liye base \(AB = 2a\). \(C(0, -b)\) ka is line se faasla (height) \(2b\) hai.
\[\tfrac{1}{2} \times 2a \times 2b = 2ab \;\checkmark\]
(Yeh \(a, b > 0\) ke liye hai; aam taur par area \(|2ab|\) hai.)
blocks.answer: \(\Delta ABC\) ka area \(2ab\) square units hai.

blocks.title: Example 15
blocks.problem: Find the area of the region bounded by the triangle with vertices \(A(1, 2)\), \(B(3, 6)\) and \(C(5, 10)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(A(1, 2)\), \(B(3, 6)\), \(C(5, 10)\).
Maloom karna: triangle \(ABC\) se ghire hue hisse ka area \(\Delta\).
Tareeqa: determinant formula. Pehle row operations se zeros banayenge taa ke expansion chhoti ho jaye.

Qadam 1: determinant likh kar \(R_1\) minus karein
\[\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 6 & 1 \\ 5 & 10 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 8 & 0 \end{vmatrix}\]
\(R_2 - R_1\) aur \(R_3 - R_1\) se.
Kyun: ek row ko doosri mein se minus karne se determinant ki value nahi badalti (yeh aap Class XI mein determinants ki properties mein parh chuke hain), aur teesre column ke 1 zero ban jate hain.

Qadam 2: teesre column ke saath expand karein
\[= \tfrac{1}{2}\left[1\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 4 & 8 \end{vmatrix}\right]\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{2}[16 - 16] = 0\]
Kyun: teesre column mein sirf upar wala entry non-zero hai; us ka sign \(+\) aur minor \(2 \cdot 8 - 4 \cdot 4 = 0\).

Qadam 3: natija
Area zero aaya, matlab yeh asal mein triangle hai hi nahi: teeno points ek hi line par hain (collinear).
Kyun: 5.7 ka Corollary: \(\Delta = 0\) tabhi hota hai jab teeno points ek line par hon.

Tasdeeq:
\[m_{AB} = \dfrac{6 - 2}{3 - 1} = 2\]
\[m_{BC} = \dfrac{10 - 6}{5 - 3} = 2\]
Dono slopes barabar aur point \(B\) dono mein common, is liye \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) ek line par hain \(\checkmark\).
blocks.answer: \(\Delta = 0\); is liye diye gaye points collinear hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahi.) Triangle \(O(0, 0)\), \(A(4, 0)\), \(B(0, 3)\) ka area nikaliye.
\[\Delta = \tfrac{1}{2}[0(0 - 3) + 4(3 - 0) + 0(0 - 0)]\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{2}(12) = 6\]
Yeh right triangle hai jis ki base 4 aur height 3 hai, aur \(\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3 = 6\). Dono tareeqon se ek hi jawab; formula par bharosa pakka!

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\Delta = \frac{1}{2}[x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)]\), ya determinant (rows \((x_i, y_i, 1)\)) ka aadha.
2. Yeh teen trapeziums se banta hai: do jama, ek minus.
3. Negative jawab ka matlab vertices clockwise liye gaye; area hamesha absolute value hai.
4. \(\Delta = 0\) agar aur sirf agar teeno points collinear hon.
5. Row operations (maslan \(R_2 - R_1\)) se zeros banaiye, expansion chhoti ho jati hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\frac{1}{2}\) bhool jana; jawab double aa jata hai.
2. Negative area likh dena; hamesha \(|\Delta|\) likhein.
3. Expansion mein signs ka ghalat pattern: row ya column ke saath \(+, -, +\).
4. Formula ke andar indices ki tarteeb bigaar dena: \(x_1(y_2 - y_3)\), \(x_2(y_3 - y_1)\), \(x_3(y_1 - y_2)\), yani 1, 2, 3 ka chakkar.
